card.name: Linking words after a noun phrase subject
card.fires_on: Small linking words (prepositions, verbs like is or brought, a period) that come right after a noun phrase in general-news or encyclopedic prose, such as 'exposure to mercury is through' or 'the price of'. The word marked is the one that links the subject to what comes next.

modes.label: Preposition after subject noun
modes.description: A preposition such as through, of, behind, from or on that follows a noun phrase about health, aid or public works.
modes.example: much human exposure to mercury is<< through>> the consumption of contaminated fish.

modes.label: Verb or copula after subject
modes.description: A verb like is or brought right after a subject noun phrase, beginning the statement about it.
modes.example: The opening of the Piccadilly Line extension in 1933<< brought>> further development to the west.

card.plain: It fires on the small connecting word that comes right after the subject of a sentence in news or history text.
